mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month percentage change) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is continuously active as long as the rate is declining.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the 3-month FEDFUNDS change is negative, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.3pp over 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month increases in the federal funds rate and CPI (each exceeding 0.5 percentage points) signal aggressive monetary tightening that overcools the economy, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise by more than 0.5pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a 1-month decline in housing starts exceeding 0.5% signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST falls by more than 0.5% in one month, or the Rank IC for the signal within the regime falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (measured as the 3-month percentage change) indicates strengthening supply conditions and economic activity, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is continuously active as long as production is rising.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% over 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month decline in non-farm payrolls exceeding 100,000 signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS declines by more than 100,000 in one month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery regime, a 1-month decline in retail sales exceeding 0.5% signals a potential return to recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-recession recovery regime, SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS falls by more than 0.5% in one month, or the Rank IC for the signal within the regime falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 1-month declines in industrial production and housing starts (each exceeding 0.5%) signal a broad-based supply slowdown, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% and HOUST falls > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both INDPRO and HOUST fall by more than 0.5% in one month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
